quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #18
										  					
  

25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: When can you drive through a yellow light?

options.text: When an emergency vehicle is crossing your lane.
When pedestrians are crossing.
When you are turning right.
When you are already in the intersection as the light turns yellow.

questions.correctAnswerText: When you are already in the intersection as the light turns yellow.
questions.explanation: If you are already in the intersection when the light turns yellow, you can continue through safely.

questions.question: Can you drive around or under a railroad crossing gate that is coming down?

options.text: Yes, if a train is not too close.
Yes, if your vehicle will not damage the gate.
Yes, if you look both ways carefully.
No, never.

questions.explanation: When lights flash, bells ring, or gates are down at a railroad crossing, stop completely. Do not cross the tracks until the lights and bells stop and the gates are fully up. Never drive around or under a gate.

questions.question: What does a red arrow on a traffic light mean?

options.text: Drive slowly through the intersection.
Stop, then go when the way is clear.
Stop and wait. Go only when the light turns green or a green arrow appears.
You can turn in the direction the arrow points.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop and wait. Go only when the light turns green or a green arrow appears.
questions.explanation: A red arrow means you must stop completely. Wait until the light turns green or a green arrow appears before you move.

questions.question: When can you text while driving?

options.text: If you are under age 18.
If you are age 18 or older.
If you can text without looking at your phone.
Only in emergencies.

questions.explanation: Do not text while driving unless it is an emergency. Looking away from the road, even for a moment, can cause a crash.

questions.question: Your wheels slip off the edge of the road. What should you do?

options.text: Jerk the steering wheel to force the vehicle back onto the road.
Speed up and steer back onto the road gradually.
Slam on the brakes and stop.
Slow down gently with the brakes and steer back onto the road slowly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down gently with the brakes and steer back onto the road slowly.
questions.explanation: Keep your wheels on the shoulder and slow down gently using the brakes. Once you reach a safe speed, turn the steering wheel to get back on the road. Do not jerk the wheel suddenly.

questions.question: How can you prevent hydroplaning?

options.text: Keep your tires in good condition with proper tread.
Keep your tires inflated to the correct pressure.
Slow down when driving in rain.
All of the above.

questions.explanation: To prevent hydroplaning, keep your tires in good condition with proper tread and correct pressure. Slow down when driving in wet weather, since hydroplaning happens more often at higher speeds.

questions.question: A driver is turning and a pedestrian is crossing without a traffic light. Who must yield?

options.text: Whoever started moving last.
The driver.
Whoever is slower.
The pedestrian.

questions.explanation: Drivers must always yield to pedestrians crossing at any intersection, with or without a crosswalk.

questions.question: What is the best way to handle a tailgater?

options.text: Speed up to increase the distance between you.
Slam on your brakes to make them back off.
Change lanes or slow down gradually to let them pass.
Ignore them.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change lanes or slow down gradually to let them pass.
questions.explanation: Watch your mirrors for tailgaters. If someone is following too closely, slow down gently and let them pass. Most rear-end crashes happen because drivers follow too closely.

questions.question: How can you stay awake on long trips?

options.text: Turn on your car radio.
Slow down.
Stop regularly to rest and stretch.
Move your eyes from side to side while driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop regularly to rest and stretch.
questions.explanation: Take regular breaks on long trips to rest and stretch. Stop even if you do not feel tired.

questions.question: What should you do if you have a tire blowout?

options.text: Take your foot off the gas.
Do not brake right away.
Slow down gradually and pull to the side of the road.
All of the above.

questions.explanation: When a tire blows out, lift your foot off the gas and do not brake suddenly. Slow down gently and pull safely off the road.

questions.question: How should you think about railroad crossings?

options.text: They are safe because trains rarely come.
They are dangerous.
They are safe places to park.
You always must stop there.

questions.explanation: Railroad crossings are always dangerous. Look and listen for trains from both directions. Follow all signs and signals. Never cross until it is safe.

questions.question: How should you merge onto a busy freeway?

options.text: Use your mirrors and check your blind spots.
Use the entrance ramp to match the speed of freeway traffic.
Yield to vehicles already on the freeway.
All of the above.

questions.explanation: Use the entrance ramp to speed up and match freeway traffic. Yield to vehicles already on the freeway. Check your mirrors and blind spots to make sure you have room to merge safely.

questions.question: What should you consider when driving near large trucks?

options.text: Large trucks need more distance to stop.
Large trucks need less distance to stop.
Large trucks are quieter.
Large trucks travel faster.

questions.correctAnswerText: Large trucks need more distance to stop.
questions.explanation: Large trucks need more distance to stop than smaller vehicles. Stay where the truck driver can see you. Do not block the truck driver's view.

questions.question: When turning onto a street with multiple lanes in your direction, which lane should you turn into?

options.text: The lane closest to the lane you came from.
The lane marked with an arrow.
The middle lane.
Any lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: The lane closest to the lane you came from.
questions.explanation: Turn into the lane closest to your previous lane. Do not change lanes while turning.

questions.question: What helps a person recover from the effects of alcohol?

options.text: Tomato juice and lime.
Hot coffee.
Fresh air.
Only time.

questions.explanation: Only time helps a person recover from alcohol's effects.

questions.question: Why does driving at night require more caution?

options.text: Traffic moves faster at night.
There is more traffic at night.
Drivers cannot see as well at night.
Accidents happen more often at night.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drivers cannot see as well at night.
questions.explanation: It is dark at night, so drivers cannot see as well. Use your headlights from 30 minutes after sunset until 30 minutes before sunrise, or whenever people or vehicles are not visible for 500 feet ahead.

questions.question: Checking your blind spot by turning your head before changing lanes or merging is:

options.text: A bad driving habit.
A good driving habit.
Unnecessary.
Not needed if you use the rearview mirror.

questions.explanation: Always check your blind spots by looking over your shoulder before changing lanes. Do not rely only on your mirrors.

questions.question: What do downward-facing triangular signs mean?

options.text: School zones ahead.
Yield to other traffic.
Construction zone ahead.
Railroad crossing ahead.

questions.explanation: Downward-facing triangular signs tell drivers to yield. You may proceed when the road is clear and safe.

questions.question: What does this sign prevent?

options.text: Entrance to full parking lots.
Entrance to road construction areas.
Entrance to dead-end streets.
Entering one-way streets and expressway ramps from the wrong direction.

questions.correctAnswerText: Entering one-way streets and expressway ramps from the wrong direction.
questions.explanation: This sign warns that the road is one-way. You cannot enter from your current direction.

questions.question: Is driving at night more or less dangerous than driving during the day?

options.text: Less dangerous.
About the same.
More dangerous.
Easier on your eyes.

questions.explanation: Night driving is more dangerous. Visibility is lower, headlight glare can temporarily blind you, and more tired or impaired drivers are on the road.

questions.question: When can you pass another vehicle?

options.text: On hills or curves because oncoming traffic will not be there.
By driving on the shoulder of the road.
If your lane has a solid yellow line and the other lane is empty.
None of the above.

questions.explanation: Do not pass on hills or curves—you cannot see oncoming cars. Do not drive on the shoulder to pass. Do not cross a solid yellow line to pass.

questions.question: A fire truck without lights or sirens is behind you on a two-lane street. What should you do?

options.text: Keep driving normally.
Stop as fast as you can.
Speed up to move out of the way.
Slow down, move right, and stop.

questions.explanation: If an emergency vehicle has no siren or flashing lights, you do not need to move. Drive normally.

questions.question: When turning left, who must you yield to?

options.text: Other drivers already in the intersection.
Cars coming toward you.
Pedestrians already in the intersection.
All of the above.

questions.explanation: When turning left, yield to cars coming toward you, pedestrians, cyclists, and other drivers in the intersection.

questions.question: You turn onto a two-lane road with a broken yellow line. What does this mean?

options.text: Traffic moves in both directions.
Traffic moves in one direction only.
The road is being repaired.
You must stay to the left of the broken yellow lines.

questions.explanation: Yellow centerlines separate traffic going in opposite directions. Broken lines can be crossed when it is safe to pass slower traffic.

questions.question: What does this black and yellow sign mean?

options.text: The road to the right is one-way only.
The road is closed to the right due to construction.
Slow down because the road ahead turns sharply.
There is a side road to your right.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down because the road ahead turns sharply.
questions.explanation: This sign shows that the road curves sharply ahead. Slow down before the turn.
